name: OneSignal
description: OneSignal is a customer-engagement platform for push notifications, in-app messages, email, SMS, live activities, journeys, and user data. Product and marketing teams use it to coordinate cross-channel messaging and measure delivery and engagement.
agentUseSummary: Add a dedicated customer-owned OneSignal App API Key and bind its exact App ID; agents can inspect a redacted first page of recent message delivery counts without content, targeting, or recipient data.

credentialRequirements.name: ONESIGNAL_APP_ID
credentialRequirements.label: OneSignal App ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use the exact UUID v4 App ID from Settings > Keys & IDs. Relay binds every request to this app.

credentialRequirements.name: ONESIGNAL_APP_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: OneSignal App API Key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Create a dedicated App API Key, preferably with an IP allowlist. Relay encrypts it and sends it only in the Authorization header to https://api.onesignal.com.

capabilities.label: Read notification delivery summaries
capabilities.description: Read page 0 of at most 25 recent message lifecycle/count summaries while excluding content, targeting, recipients, templates, URLs, media, outcomes, and raw provider data.

approvalRequired.label: List OneSignal notification delivery summaries
approvalRequired.description: Return at most 25 recent message IDs, lifecycle timestamps, cancellation state, and aggregate delivery counts with content and audience data removed.

blocked.label: Access message content, targeting, or outcomes
blocked.description: Names, headings, contents, custom data, segments, filters, aliases, recipients, templates, URLs, media, platform delivery detail, outcomes, and raw messages remain blocked.

blocked.label: Access users, subscriptions, or exports
blocked.description: Users, aliases, external IDs, subscriptions, devices, tags, properties, segments, custom events, CSV exports, Event Streams, and recipient history remain blocked.

blocked.label: Send, cancel, write, or administer OneSignal
blocked.description: Push/email/SMS/in-app sends, cancellation, users/subscriptions/events, segments/templates, apps, API keys, webhooks, journeys, live activities, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: Arbitrary origins, apps, paths, methods, headers, queries, bodies, kinds, templates, offsets, cursors, automatic pagination, retries, SDK surfaces, raw responses, browser sessions, and bulk/export operations remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded delivery-summary read requires approval; content, targeting, users, exports, sends, cancellation, writes, administration, arbitrary APIs, pagination, and bulk remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same bounded read runs directly; exact app binding, fixed endpoint, redaction, page/result caps, audits, rate limits, and provider authorization remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one fixed OneSignal delivery-summary wrapper with exact App ID binding and message/audience redaction.
Hermes receives the same fixed OneSignal delivery-summary wrapper with exact App ID binding and message/audience redaction.

providerSetup.blocker: OneSignal REST access requires an eligible customer app and a customer-created secret App API Key whose authority can also send messages and manage users.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer admin creates a dedicated App API Key, configures an IP allowlist when available, supplies the exact App ID, and completes a live read-only connection check.

evidence.supports: OneSignal documents UUID v4 App IDs, secret single-app App API Keys, Key-scheme authorization, key rotation/deletion, separate organization keys, and optional IP allowlisting.
OneSignal documents GET /notifications with required app_id, App API Key authorization, descending queued_at order, limit/offset pagination, and an identity/content/targeting-rich response.
OneSignal documents a one-request-per-second per-app limit for view endpoints, 429 Retry-After behavior, and separate high-impact send/application message limits.
OneSignal documents broad messaging, user, subscription, segment, export, and app-management API surfaces; Relay mounts only the bounded read wrapper.

securityNotes: The App API Key is encrypted as a secret reference and sent only as Authorization: Key to https://api.onesignal.com; the UUID v4 App ID is exact-bound on the connection.
Relay allowlists only GET /notifications with fixed app_id, limit=25, offset=0, rejects redirects, uses a 30-second timeout, caps responses at 1 MB, and performs no retries or pagination.

The result includes at most 25 UUID message references, lifecycle timestamps, cancellation state, and aggregate delivery counts; it excludes names, content, data, targeting, recipients, templates, URLs, media, platform detail, outcomes, cursors, and raw responses.

Users, subscriptions, aliases, events, segments, exports, sends, cancellation, templates, apps, keys, webhooks, journeys, live activities, writes, administration, arbitrary APIs, SDKs, pagination, and bulk remain blocked.
Provider 401/403/429 and server errors are surfaced safely; key creation/capture, IP allowlisting, provider-console work, and live acceptance remain customer/external steps.
